literal: Than destroying virtue and doing evil deeds, it is indeed worse to ruin someone behind their back and smile falsely.
translation: Worse than destroying virtue and committing evil deeds is slandering someone behind their back and then smiling falsely to their face.
modern: அறத்தை அழித்துத் தீமைகளைச் செய்வதை விட, ஒருவரைப் பின்னால் பழித்துப் பேசிவிட்டு நேரில் பொய்மையாகச் சிரிப்பது மிகவும் தீமையானது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the extreme deceitfulness of backbiting. The author compares two wrongs: destroying virtue to commit evil deeds, and slandering someone behind their back while pretending to be friendly to their face. The latter is declared to be far worse. The words 'புறன் அழீஇ' (ruining behind the back) and 'பொய்த்து நகை' (smiling falsely) vividly depict the hypocrisy of a backbiter, showing that betrayal of trust is more damaging than open vice.
